text: Welcome to This is My Architecture. Today we're going to be talking about using SAP on AWS to
move towards real-time closing. I'm joined by Serena Vast from Liberty Mutual Insurance. Welcome,
Serena. What does Liberty Mutual Insurance do? Liberty Mutual helps people preserve and protect
what they earn, build, own and cherish. Fantastic. And so what does real-time closing mean? Why are
you working towards that? Real-time close means the business people doesn't need to wait for any
time to close the books at the end of the month. So it means they can get answers quicker and more
easily? Yes, that's correct. You know, today in our previous world, they wait for 10 days to close
the books. So the goal is to close the books, continuous close of the books. So you built a
new architecture here based on SAP to really uplift your capability from your old systems. Talk us
through what you've built here. Before this migration, we have our SAP world systems running
in on-prem, SAPs, ECC and BPC. The goal was to migrate those systems onto the AWS. So we have
all of our policy systems and claim systems and reinsurance systems running on-prem through an ETL layer.
They ingest data into S3 on a scheduled basis. That data finally ends up in HANA, S4 HANA,
on a scheduled basis for further processing by our financial enders. So let's draw that flow so we can
sort of see how it's going through. So you've got data coming from your ETL into S3 and then that's
loading into the HANA database. And how often is that taking place? Today, based upon the source system,
it could be at the end of the month or it could be on a weekly basis from the source systems to S3. But
it is always from S3 to our S4 HANA landscape on an end of the month basis. But in the real-time
closing concept, that's going to be more event based? Exactly. So in a real-time close scenario,
so the source systems would be producing events. Those events would be sourced into S4 HANA on a real-time
basis. And talk to me about this component here. So what I have here is my high availability topology.
The boxes, the two boxes up here, AppServer and HANA, and the same configuration is supported on the other side.
So we're, we have HANA replication set up between the primary database server and the secondary database
server to support the failover onto my secondary server. And you're running on the X1 family for EC2 here?
That's correct. So we have X132 instances running to support my HANA database up here.
And what sort of performance improvement did you see moving to that particular architecture?
Prior to this migration, the currency translations used to take like 10 hours. And they are taking under an
hour now. That's a huge win for us, which is also allowing us to achieve that faster close of the books.
And also our financial analysts are able to create ad hoc reports in minutes before they were taking more than,
you know, a longer time.
So way more capacity there. And I also see you've got a DR solution also built in here as well.
Right. So we have defined cross region replication of the backups and snapshots from our primary to the
secondary region to support the build out of the disaster recovery infrastructure.
So I notice here you've got cloud formation and cloud watch. What are you using those for in this architecture?
The cloud formation is to automate the build out of the infrastructure. And also the cloud formation is supported through a bamboo pipeline to schedule the build outs of this infrastructure.
The cloud watch is allowing us to define thresholds and monitor this infrastructure for those key events.
And how long does it take the cloud formation templates to build out this SAP landscape?
It's about under an hour. We can build this whole primary and the secondary and all this topology.
And what did that use to take in terms of build time?
Probably, I would say months. So as an example, we were able to share our cloud formation artifacts with other business units in Liberty Mutual.
So they were able to create their own S4 HANA infrastructure in days as opposed to months.
So you've moved from months to days in terms of building your own environments and have the ability to clone them as well.
That's correct.
That's fantastic. Shrunabhas, thanks so much for sharing that with us today.
Thank you.
And thank you so much for watching. This is My Architecture.
